- Plausible self-hosts its ClickHouse database and PostgreSQL instances. (source: https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFVQBeIYGN1eCZuEfmjTUUYrRGhdLqUJJc1FgRvAcgyVtZm-Wpy2IqQgkhZbyh6f3o89fUMJt7Lv4D0vfTMxBan0aDOFeoF26yNGMsYQStDy910s_N1lwhdAh1e7F15e6YDKcccU-sW) (quote: "We self-host our Clickhouse database and plan to start self-hosting our PostgreSQL instance as well.")
- Plausible deploys workloads using Docker on Hetzner Cloud servers running Ubuntu. (source: https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFVQBeIYGN1eCZuEfmjTUUYrRGhdLqUJJc1FgRvAcgyVtZm-Wpy2IqQgkhZbyh6f3o89fUMJt7Lv4D0vfTMxBan0aDOFeoF26yNGMsYQStDy910s_N1lwhdAh1e7F15e6YDKcccU-sW) (quote: "We currently deploy our workloads with plain Docker on Hetzner Cloud servers running Ubuntu.")
- Plausible's self-hosted Community Edition is distributed under the AGPLv3 open-source license. (source: https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGT7jOqwkOY_wQVTqtRfcwbkJy3t7YDm3ie9aqfeTx2bMNv0UCjyq6fR79QR-d1QMLlyvNBKsyL57d8uhC_k6rIyj3-PgzUEjbvJurLLDQ2GgEQPyeeWUdI1Neq89aeGXux7Pfa) (quote: "It is built on the same open source codebase (AGPLv3), though some features are available on Plausible Cloud only.")

## Business pains
- Aggressive ad blockers can block Plausible despite its privacy-friendly model because they target all analytics tools indiscriminately. (source: https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFlEj8GkB53GkvCdb99QmyyToNBFTXgPG5Rnsv3lYd-bhQMGOipWDD-XNOrZ37RshMN9CSa4om3jTC13LsTn403Y8ftEktjyMYep3isohiuIlG69J52puT0H5slYSaAfGht-DKYZIvKCpSc6tm4cyUYLdqLvivo7hU=) (quote: "Some aggressive blockers can still block Plausible because they block all analytics tools, not just privacy-invasive ones.")
- Vertically scaling single servers reached operational limits under high-volume event ingestion. (source: https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFVQBeIYGN1eCZuEfmjTUUYrRGhdLqUJJc1FgRvAcgyVtZm-Wpy2IqQgkhZbyh6f3o89fUMJt7Lv4D0vfTMxBan0aDOFeoF26yNGMsYQStDy910s_N1lwhdAh1e7F15e6YDKcccU-sW) (quote: "We are starting to hit the limits of our current setup where we just scale cloud servers vertically.")
- Providing technical support to open-source self-hosters in the same manner as paying subscribers proved impossible to sustain. (source: https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFCwexr2S5KHk1S3W4FWlU1Y_cvOgoexhmBrdsIPuKZ99vt0JGgAFr450oFqfIFpuVRMKikTs3u3P8DTlLVnFOKWF8DZZcTnsFoppG7soN8GDwWJkaefhPuBJjnabj-SgMLaLdG-sVqvQ==) (quote: "Early on, we tried to deal with self-hosting questions in the same way as questions from our paying subscribers. That turned out to be an impossible task")
- Standard Google Analytics remains available without any subscription fee. (source: https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQF-5Lnsxn3WAOvHZuOmyU_6VaIuxtM1SQ7LZjDSl3C6hzkw9gsSLCd3Q8zTbFb1I7WtwsKUMifdiwa3t_QCIfXJg8VRu3pXGPdoQ0r3ultMapMoJHpkB_nS_f6Wy6uinRcfXF9dVVGAlQ==) (quote: "Standard Google Analytics has no subscription fee. You can use it for a business website without buying GA360.")
- Hypothesis: Plausible faces constant positioning hurdles having to persuade prospective customers to pay for analytics when Google Analytics provides standard web analytics for free. (based on: Standard Google Analytics remains available without any subscription fee.)
- Hypothesis: Ad blockers blocking Plausible's script by default lead to data underreporting concerns and increased customer support inquiries. (based on: Aggressive ad blockers can block Plausible despite its privacy-friendly model because they target all analytics tools indiscriminately.)
- Hypothesis: Scaling the ingestion pipeline horizontally across clusters presents complex architectural and operational demands for a small engineering team. (based on: Vertically scaling single servers reached operational limits under high-volume event ingestion.)
- Hypothesis: Maintaining the free self-hosted Community Edition creates non-revenue-generating support overhead that risks pulling engineering resources away from paying SaaS customers. (based on: Providing technical support to open-source self-hosters in the same manner as paying subscribers proved impossible to sustain.)
